records.name_note: Sources split structurally but converge on the same lead name. NC State's Common Name(s) field is a four-entry alphabetized list (Big Bluestem, Bluestem, Broomsedge, Turkey Foot) whose first entry also matches the page title, and NC State's own body prose opens with "Big bluestem"; Missouri Botanical Garden's Plant Finder carries one Common Name value, "Big bluestem", with no Common Names list behind it, and mentions "turkeyfoot grass" only in prose as "the additional common name"; RHS's plant-profile subtitle reads "big blue stem", with "beard grass, shepherd's beard" under Other common names. UGA's Native Plants for Georgia Part IV (a multi-species publication, not a dedicated single-species page) heads its section "Big Bluestem, Turkeyfoot / Andropogon gerardii", co-listing Turkeyfoot rather than establishing a rival lead. Spelling: NC State and MoBot both spell the epithet "Andropogon gerardi" (one i) in their headings and prose, while RHS's Name Status field affirms "Andropogon gerardii" (two i's, the given spelling) as Correct and lists "Andropogon furcatus" as a synonym.
unknowns: No admissible source (NC State, MoBot, RHS, Clemson HGIC, Penn State, UMD, UGA) addresses toxicity to cats or dogs for Andropogon gerardii, so toxic_to_pets and toxicity_detail are left null. NC State's page for this species carries no Poison Severity/Poison Part fields at all.

soil_drainage left null: NC State's Soil Drainage tags span both 'Occasionally Dry' and 'Occasionally Wet' (moderate per the rubric), and Penn State/UGA prose describe 'moist, well-drained' cultivation (also moderate) — but RHS's cultivation sentence explicitly calls for 'light, sharply-drained, preferably sandy soil' and states it 'Will not tolerate excessive winter wet,' a genuine conflict with the moist-tolerant reading, so the field is left null rather than resolved either way.

soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max left null: NC State's page for this species has no Soil pH field at all, and RHS's pH field lists 'Acid or Alkaline or Neutral' — since RHS accepts both acid and alkaline soils, per the ceiling/floor rule both bounds are left null.

water_regime left null: no admissible source frames a watering statement in dry-down terms for this species. MoBot's structured 'Water: Dry to medium' field is mid-scale and is disclosed only as a counterpoint, not used to populate the enum.

direct_sun_hours_max left null: NC State's '6 or more hours of direct sunlight a day' figure is the generic text embedded in its site-wide Light-category legend, not species-specific prose, so it was not used.

outdoor_sun_exposure excludes part_sun/part_shade even though UMD ('Full sun to part shade') and UGA ('prefers full sun to partial shade') mention shade tolerance in prose, because NC State, MoBot, and RHS — the three sources with structured sun fields — each list only full sun.

records.name_note: Sources split on which common name leads, and each has a distinct page structure. NC State's Common Name(s) field lists American Feverfew, Eastern Feverfew, Wild Quinine in alphabetical order, and its first entry, American Feverfew, is also the first name in the page title; NC State's own body prose, however, calls the plant 'Wild Quinine' throughout. Missouri Botanical Garden's Plant Finder carries an affirmative single-value 'Common Name:' field reading 'wild quinine', and its Common Names popup lists wild quinine first, then American feverfew, cutting almond, prairie dock; MoBot's own prose opens 'commonly called American feverfew or wild quinine'. RHS's plant-profile subtitle (and page title) leads with 'American feverfew', with 'cutting almond, prairie dock, wild quinine' on one line under Other common names. Of the three dedicated single-species pages, only MoBot leads with wild quinine; NC State's title and alphabetized list lead with American Feverfew while its body prose uses Wild Quinine throughout; RHS leads with American feverfew. Wild Quinine is used here on the strength of MoBot's affirmative Common Name field and NC State's prose, with American feverfew recorded as a genuine and arguably stronger lead-name split.
unknowns: No page across the ten admissible domains (NC State, Clemson HGIC, MoBot Plant Finder, UF/IFAS EDIS, UF/IFAS Ask IFAS, RHS, Penn State Extension, U Maryland Extension, UGA fieldreport.caes.uga.edu) carries a toxicity, poison, or contact-dermatitis statement for Parthenium integrifolium specifically (unlike the well-documented parthenium dermatitis caused by the related weed Parthenium hysterophorus, which is out of scope for this species). NC State's page has no Poison block and no 'Poisonous' Plant Type tag or 'Poisonous to Humans' Problems tag for this species. toxic_to_pets and toxicity_detail are left null accordingly.

soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max are left null: NC State's Soil pH field lists a closed 'Neutral (6.0-8.0)' band alongside an open-ended 'Alkaline (>8.0)' band, which would suggest a 6.0 floor, but RHS's pH field explicitly accepts 'Acid, alkaline, or neutral' soils -- since RHS lists both acid and alkaline soils as acceptable, both the floor and the ceiling are voided per the cross-check rule.

outdoor_sun_exposure excludes part_shade even though RHS's Position field states 'Full sun or partial shade,' because NC State's Light field and MoBot's Sun field structurally list only Full sun (this is the typical UK-calibrated RHS tolerance the rules flag for exclusion).

water_regime (dry_thoroughly_between) is a soft read of MoBot's structured 'Water: Dry to medium' field; no admissible source frames watering with an explicit 'let it dry out' or 'keep evenly moist' instruction, so treat this value with some caution.

No admissible source states day/night temperature ranges, humidity percentage or category, chill-damage onset temperature, light in foot-candles, a species-specific direct-sun-hours maximum (NC State's hour figure is its site-wide light-category legend, excluded by rule), or any fertilizing schedule/strength for this species -- all left null.

Searches of hgic.clemson.edu, extension.umd.edu, edis.ifas.ufl.edu, ask.ifas.ufl.edu, and fieldreport.caes.uga.edu turned up only passing mentions of Parthenium integrifolium (garden photo galleries, a forest-farming publication listing) with no care-relevant structured data, and no University of Maryland Extension page on this species was found at all.

records.name_note: Sources converge on "purple poppy mallow" as the working name but present it differently. NC State's Common Name(s) field is a four-entry alphabetized list -- Finger Poppy Mallow, Poppy Mallow, Purple Poppy Mallow, Winecup -- and the page title repeats those four names in the same order, so NC State's list leads with Finger Poppy Mallow; NC State's Description prose, however, uses "Purple poppy mallow" throughout ("Purple poppy mallow prefers full sun in well-drained moist to occasionally dry soil."), which is the name adopted here. NC State also has a per-common-name page for each listed name, each titled "<Name> - Callirhoe involucrata" (e.g. Winecup, Poppy Mallow). MoBot's dedicated page leads with "Common Name: purple poppy mallow"; a longer Common Names list sits behind a popup whose text exists only in the link's markup, so it is not quoted here. RHS's H1 is the botanical name alone, its page title and profile subtitle read "Callirhoe involucrata | purple poppy mallow", and a separate "Other common names" heading lists buffalo rose, crimson-flowered poppy mallow, wine cup, winecups. NC State's "is often confused with:" module (Callirhoe bushii, Callirhoe digitata) confirms this record is scoped to C. involucrata.
unknowns: No admissible source (NC State, MoBot, or the fetched RHS page) carries a Poisonous plant-type tag, a Poison block, or any cats/dogs-scoped toxicity statement for Callirhoe involucrata, so toxic_to_pets and toxicity_detail are left null.

No admissible source states a numeric damage-onset temperature or a cool-rest cultivation note for this species; NC State's USDA Plant Hardiness Zone 4a-8b is a survival/growing-range rating, not a chill-damage-onset figure, so chill_damage_f and cool_rest_note are left null per the rule against deriving damage onset from a hardiness rating.

None of the three admissible sources fetched give numeric day/night temperature ranges, humidity percentages, or foot-candle light figures for this species, so day_f_min/max, night_f_min/max, humidity_need, humidity_pct_min/max, light_fc_min, and light_fc_good are left null.

NC State's Light field text '(6 or more hours of direct sunlight a day)' is the site-wide legend definition attached to the Full sun category rather than species-specific prose, so it was not used for direct_sun_hours_max, which is left null.

Neither NC State (which has no Soil pH field on this species' page) nor RHS (whose soil/pH cultivation fields did not render in the fetched page content for this species) state a pH range, so soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max are left null.

No admissible source frames watering for this in-ground perennial as a regime statement: MoBot's structured field reads 'Water: Dry to medium,' a mid/dry-scale descriptor rather than a keep_moist-style instruction, and NC State's Culture text gives only a soil-moisture/drainage descriptor ('well-drained moist to occasionally dry soil'), not a watering instruction. water_regime, water_dry_down_target, water_check_depth_cm, water_growing_days_est, and water_dormant_days_est are left null per the rule that these day-interval/target fields stay null for an in-ground perennial unless a source frames watering that way.
